A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RECAST framework, RECAST-30K dataset and RLVC training approach. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, constraint and component ablations, RLVC training dynamics, dataset analyses and human evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark, ablation and human-evaluation results and additionally reports seed-domain counts, construction-cost estimates and expanded training-dynamics measurements.

M1.justification: Constraint extraction, filtering, instruction and response selection, binary verification, averaged constraint rewards and GRPO optimization remain unchanged. The revised 19-type description matches the nine rule-based and ten model-based categories already listed in v3 Tables 6–7; it does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v4 removes BBH and MMLU-PRO throughout the paper, substantially narrowing coverage of heterogeneous reasoning tasks and broad multitask knowledge. RECAST-Test, IFEval, FollowBench, GPQA and MuSR remain. The new seed-domain breakdown describes the existing Tülu 3 Persona IF source rather than added training coverage.

E2.justification: The eight dataset baselines remain Conifer, CRaB, I-SHEEP, MUFFIN, ShareGPT, Evol-Instruct, Suri and Tülu 3 Persona IF. Table 1 also retains the same large-model comparators, and comparator membership is unchanged within the retained external benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported constraint-type ablation narrows from Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B to Llama alone. External results now use separate two-benchmark averages instead of one six-benchmark average. RECAST-Test construction, individual benchmark metrics, training settings and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: v4 adds seed-domain and construction-cost analyses and expands existing RLVC dynamics analysis with model-based rewards and MSR measurements. It removes the Qwen constraint-type ablation panels from v3 Figure 4. Constraint-count and component ablations remain, relocated to Appendix D.6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained GRPO group-standard-deviation formula concerns optimization rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All BBH and MMLU-PRO results and the Qwen constraint-type ablation curves are removed. v4 adds seed-domain counts, a $175 construction-cost estimate and model-based training trajectories; Table 8 also reports rule-reward checkpoints differing from v3 Figure 5. Table 1 and individual scores on the four retained external benchmarks are unchanged. New benchmark averages summarize different subsets, not performance gains.

T1.justification: The verification function, constraint-reward definition, HSR formula and GRPO objective and advantage equations are mathematically unchanged. GRPO's formulation moves from v3 Section 4.3 to v4 Appendix D.5; no new theorem, proof or formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The three central RECAST, RECAST-30K and RLVC contributions remain. v4 adds explicit low-cost and scalability claims, specifies that prior datasets do not exceed ten constraints, and highlights Llama-3.1-8B outperforming Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. General-capability preservation is elevated to the abstract, extending the emphasis without replacing the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix F's substantive limitations concerning verification overhead, interacting constraints, imperfect subjective validators and predominantly English evaluation disappear. v4 adds an interpretation that RLVC first learns easier model-based constraints before shifting toward harder rule-based objectives, and interprets external benchmark performance as evidence against overfitting. These substantially change the paper's qualifications and explanatory account.

D1.justification: v4 adds per-stage construction-cost estimates and a conditional plan to release code, data and trained models upon acceptance, alongside an expanded pipeline walkthrough. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, API settings and prompt templates remain. The release statement does not establish that additional resources are already available.

R1.justification: v4 adds Wang et al.'s autonomous-agent survey and sharper contrasts with manually constructed datasets and AutoIF's code-verifiable constraints. Several broader instruction-tuning references and the BBH/MMLU-PRO references are removed. The principal related-work comparisons remain; publication updates for retained papers are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves after experiments, while GRPO details and ablations move into appendices. v4 adds a dedicated pipeline appendix and ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements, alongside title, author-list and terminology edits. This materially reorganizes the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 Table 2 becomes two narrower tables, new domain and cost tables appear, and the RLVC curve is replaced by a numerical table. The constraint-type figure loses its Qwen panels, and an enlarged repeat of the pipeline diagram is added. These changes accompany extensive reformatting and relocation of displays; the constraint-distribution and prompt figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the pipeline explanation, reconciles taxonomy counts and adds useful resource information. However, removing BBH/MMLU-PRO evidence and the substantive limitations weakens readers' ability to assess its retained capability-preservation and scalability claims. These losses in evidential coverage and qualification outweigh the documentation gains, producing a limited overall decline while the central method and benchmark results remain intact.
